anomalies.observed: The AVR-ISP-6 programming header J4 carries local labels MISO (pin 1), MOSI (pin 4) and SCK (pin 3); these names appear nowhere else on the sheet. The microcontroller ISP pins (U2/U3 pins 5, 6, 7 = PB0/PB1/PB2) carry the labels SDA, PWM and SCL instead, so J4 pins 1, 3 and 4 are single-node nets with no path to the MCU. Only RST (J4.5), VCC (J4.2) and GND (J4.6) are actually connected.
anomalies.expected: An AVR ISP header must be wired to the target's ISP pins, i.e. J4 MOSI/MISO/SCK should share nets with PB0/PB1/PB2 (the SDA/PWM/SCL nets at U2/U3). With different label names on the two ends, no such connection exists.

evidence.quote: J4 AVR-ISP-6 right-side pins labelled MISO (1), MOSI (4), SCK (3), RST (5) - sheet 1, root
U2 ATtiny45-20P pins 5/6/7 = AREF/PB0 -> SDA, PB1 -> PWM, PB2 -> SCL; U3 ATtiny13V-10S pins 5/6/7 = PB0 -> SDA, PB1 -> PWM, PB2 -> SCK - sheet 1, right

anomalies.impact: The ISP header cannot program the ATtiny in-system; the MCU's MOSI/MISO/SCK pins are floating at the header, so J4 is effectively non-functional for programming.

anomalies.observed: R3 (10K) and R6 (10K) are drawn with their top ends on the VCC rail and their bottom ends on the RST and TACH nets respectively. The ATtiny reset pin (U2/U3 pin 1 = RESET/PB5) sits on RST and the tach input (U2/U3 pin 3 = PB4) sits on TACH, while the ATtiny supply pin 8 is tied to +5V. U1 (LM1117-5.0) has VIN = VCC and VOUT = +5V, so VCC is the unregulated input rail (higher than 5 V).
anomalies.expected: Pull-ups that feed an MCU input (reset and tach) must reference the MCU's own supply, +5 V, not the pre-regulator VCC rail; otherwise the pin is pulled above the ATtiny's absolute-maximum rating.

evidence.quote: R3 10K and R6 10K, top ends on the VCC label, bottoms on RST and TACH - sheet 1, root
U1 LM1117-5.0: pin 3 VIN = VCC, pin 2 VOUT = +5V; U2/U3 pin 8 VCC = +5V - sheet 1, right

anomalies.impact: The RST and TACH nets are pulled to the raw VCC rail instead of the 5 V MCU rail. The ATtiny reset and tach inputs are over-driven above their absolute maximum, risking clamp-diode current, unreliable reset and damaged/latched I/O; the tach pull-up level is also wrong for the logic threshold.

parsed.summary: The build deviates from the intended fan-controller design in two places: the AVR-ISP-6 header's MISO/MOSI/SCK pins are not connected to the ATtiny's ISP pins (they carry unmatched net names), and the reset/tach pull-ups R3/R6 are tied to the unregulated VCC rail rather than the ATtiny's +5V supply, over-driving those MCU pins.
